title: Structured-output contract telemetry and delta-based gating for model/config changes
creator: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: We need a lightweight, real-time telemetry and gating system that detects regressions in structured outputs (JSON-like contracts) when model variants or serving configs change. Current alerts are token-level or holistic quality scores; they miss subtle contract-level regressions such as missing required keys, type changes, enum drift, and structural nesting errors that break downstream parsers. This ticket scopes design and implementation of: (1) a set of contract-focused evals that run on commit/config-change triggers; (2) delta scoring that attributes changes to a model/config delta; (3) a telemetry pipeline that stores per-route, per-model contract pass/fail rates over time; and (4) thresholded gates and alerting integrated with rollouts/canaries. The goal is to catch contract regressions before they reach user traffic and to provide actionable traces (example prompts, outputs, commit/config metadata) to engineers and PMs.
acceptance_criteria: A commit or config change can trigger a focused structured-output eval run (pre-deploy) that exercises the same prompt corpus used for regression evals
Per-route contract metrics are stored in our telemetry store (Grafana/Prometheus/ClickHouse) with daily and per-release granularity
Delta scoring computes change in contract-pass-rate (absolute and relative) and flags if change exceeds configurable thresholds (default: absolute drop >2% or relative drop >10%)
An automated gating webhook can fail a canary rollout when a flagged regression is observed and attach artifacts (sample input, new output, baseline output, model/config diff, PR link)
Dashboard tiles for structured-output regressions are available in the Console: per-model, per-route, by schema rule (missing-required, type-mismatch, enum-drift, extra-keys)
Documentation (Console help + internal runbook) describing how thresholds work, how to interpret alerts, and how to add new contract checks is published and reviewed by PM and Design
implementation_plan: 1) Define a canonical contract test schema DSL that maps to existing JSON Schemas but supports lighter 'soft' checks (required, type, enum, max-depth, prefix-key checks)
2) Extend eval harness to run the contract checks as lightweight binary pass/fail per sample and emit structured metrics (labels: model, model_version, route, commit_sha, config_id)
3) Add trigger: pipeline that launches eval job on model/package publish, on dedciated capacity config changes, and on PRs that modify serving/runtime config files
4) Build telemetry ingestion: lightweight events into ClickHouse (or existing metric store) with daily aggregates and windowed deltas
5) Implement delta-scoring service that computes baseline vs candidate pass rates and produces alert decisions with confidence estimation (sample sizes, bootstrap CI), and stores comparison artifacts
6) Integrate with rollout controller: show regression status in Canary UI and support optional automatic abort when high-confidence regressions are detected
7) Expose Console dashboards and incident runbook links for triage, and add a short help doc for adding new contract checks
8) Run closed pilot with 2 internal teams (Console, API) for one release cycle, iterate based on feedback
tradeoffs_and_notes: Cost vs coverage: running full eval corpus on every commit is expensive. We'll prioritize a small focused corpus per-route (50-200 samples) and support on-demand full runs for high-risk changes

Strictness: immutable/strict checks (fail on any missing required key) vs tolerant checks (thresholded tolerances). Default is conservative (fail on meaningful drops) but checks can be toggled per-route
Attribution: a config change may interact with model behavior. We'll ship best-effort attribution (config delta + commit meta) initially and consider causal inference later
Latency: the gating eval should complete within the typical CI window (<15 minutes). For heavy checks we provide asynchronous post-deploy monitoring with canary rollbacks
Privacy: examples used for telemetry will avoid PII; route owners must ensure prompt sets comply with data policies

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives on tolerant outputs could cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: use statistical confidence intervals and require sustained regression over two consecutive runs before auto-abort
Risk: High compute cost for many routes. Mitigation: tier routes by traffic and sensitivity; run preflight only on high-impact routes and daily background jobs for low-impact ones
Risk: Owners may not have representative prompt sets. Mitigation: provide tooling to generate synthetic prompts from historical traffic and allow owners to upload curated corpora
